question: A glaucoma patient is prescribed both timolol 0.5% and latanoprost 0.005% eye drops. The CORRECT counselling regarding the order and timing of these drops is:

answers.text: Instil both drops simultaneously from a combined vial to improve compliance

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Timolol and latanoprost are available as a fixed combination (Xalacom), but when prescribed separately they must not be mixed in a vial by the patient — this risks contamination and inaccurate dosing.

answers.text: Instil one drop, wait at least 5 minutes, then instil the other drop

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The 5-minute interval allows the first drop to be absorbed and excess fluid to drain before the second drop is instilled. If drops are given without a delay, the second drop washes out the first, reducing bioavailability of both medications.

answers.text: Instil both drops at the same time in different eyes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both drops are prescribed for the same eye(s) — applying each to a different eye would mean neither eye receives both medications as prescribed.

answers.text: Wait 30 minutes between drops to allow complete corneal absorption

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 30 minutes is unnecessarily long and reduces compliance. A 5-minute interval is both sufficient for bioavailability and practical for daily adherence.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key counselling point: when multiple eye drops are prescribed, instil them 5 minutes apart. This prevents the second drop from flushing out the first before it is absorbed. Poor compliance with this rule is a common cause of inadequate IOP control in glaucoma patients.
Correct. The 5-minute rule between sequential topical drops is standard counselling in ophthalmology. It preserves the bioavailability of both agents and prevents dilution washout.
